name: The Evens
label: Dischord
lede: [[Ian MacKaye]] turned the volume down, sat behind a baritone guitar across from [[Amy Farina]]'s drums, and found that two people in a barn, a museum or a theater lobby could hit harder than most bands with a wall of amps.

eras.title: Two people and one quiet room
eras.text: Ian MacKaye had spent two decades at the loud end of Washington music, from Minor Threat to Fugazi. With Amy Farina, drummer in The Warmers, he started something built on restraint: one baritone guitar, one drum kit, two voices trading lines.

years.h: Two people, one baritone guitar, no bass
years.p: [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and [[Amy Farina|30d1b9a6-4156-49ec-84ba-65c3f5ebbf69]] start playing together in Washington as the Evens. Dischord's description is short: he plays baritone guitar, she plays drums, they both sing.
years.xp:
The band took shape while [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] was winding down its touring life. Fugazi played its last shows in 2002 and went on what its members call an indefinite hiatus. The Evens ran on the opposite design: no bass, no second guitar, and a volume that let the words through.

Farina came up in [[The Warmers|af0dea4e-c501-47f2-8695-129f254d425f]] with Ian's brother [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]]. She and MacKaye were also a couple, and later married, so the band and the household were the same two people. That shaped what came after.

years.h: Before any record, the Evens show up on a kids' TV show
years.p: Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina play their song Vowel Movement for Pancake Mountain, the D.C. internet children's show. It is the band's first release, and it comes before any album.

eras.title: Quiet enough to play anywhere
eras.text: Two records in twenty months, The Evens and Get Evens, and a tour map that skipped the club circuit. Low volume meant MacKaye and Farina could set up in galleries, barns and lobbies, rooms where the audience had to listen.

yt: Around the Corner, live in Stroudsburg, PA, May 2005
years.h: The Evens is cut at Inner Ear for Dischord No. 150
years.p: Recorded in June 2004 with [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]]: twelve songs, 37 minutes, and a caged elephant silhouette on the cover.
years.xp:
Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina co-produced the record with Zientara, who had engineered Dischord bands since the label's first days. The cover photo is by Lely Constantinople, with art by [[Jason Farrell|f458f662-c72b-485b-9152-81eda8659fdb]].

The Washington Post filed it under post-post-hardcore. AllMusic heard a major leap for MacKaye.

years.cap: Ian MacKaye on baritone guitar and Amy Farina on drums, March 2007
q: Turning down allowed us to play basically anywhere.
yt: The Evens, full set, Stroudsburg, PA, May 22, 2005
years.h: Barns, museums, galleries and theater lobbies
years.p: The Evens play rooms most punk bands never see. Ian MacKaye told NPR the low volume was the point.
years.xp:
MacKaye has said that for most of his career the only rooms that would book his music were bars, places whose economy, as he put it, runs largely on self-destruction. Turning down freed the band from that. In a strange room, he told NPR, the music has to rise to meet it.

Over the next years the band toured Europe, South America, Oceania, Canada and the United States, according to Dischord.

yt: Cut From the Cloth, live, December 2006
years.h: Get Evens is recorded in the Dischord House basement
years.p: For the second album the Evens skip the studio and set up in the basement of the Dischord House in Arlington. Dischord releases it as No. 160.
years.xp:
The band mixed Get Evens at Inner Ear with Don Zientara. Ten songs, from Cut From the Cloth to Dinner With the President.

Pitchfork gave it 7.8, and Mojo, Spin and Uncut were positive. The LP was re-cut in 2010.

eras.title: Six years, one son, one record
eras.text: Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina's son arrived in 2008 and the Evens' clock changed. With both parents in the band, rehearsal, touring and bedtime ran off the same calendar, and six years passed between Get Evens and The Odds.

years.big: "He does like our music; he's also not too shy to critique things."
years.h: A son, and a critic in the audience
years.p: Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina have a son in 2008. Farina told NPR in 2012 what he thought of the band at age four.
years.xp: The Evens kept going at a pace set by family life. Talking to NPR that winter, Farina was frank about the logistics of a two-parent band, and said she and MacKaye were lucky to have family nearby.

years.cap: Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina on a small lamp-lit stage, April 2013
years.h: 2 Songs: Warble Factor and Timothy Wright for seven dollars
years.p: A seven-inch on Dischord No. 170, recorded at Inner Ear in August 2011. Both songs turn up again on The Odds a year later.
years.xp: The Evens produced the session themselves, and [[TJ Lipple|ed4cd729-b4d2-4016-a0b6-c362b68d2afb]] mastered it.

yt: The Evens at the Vex, Los Angeles, April 17, 2013
years.p: Thirteen songs, opening with King of Kings and closing with a reprise called KOK. Metacritic logged universal acclaim, Pitchfork gave it 8.0, and Stereogum put it at No. 45 on its albums of 2012.
years.xp:
Critics heard parenthood all through The Odds. AllMusic's Fred Thomas called the record refined and understated. Not every song landed: several reviewers singled out Competing With the Till as the clumsy one.

Talking to NPR, Amy Farina said their four-year-old son was a fan with opinions.

eras.title: A bass player joins the kitchen band
eras.text: After The Odds in 2012 the Evens went quiet on record. MacKaye and Farina kept playing, and in 2015 they started jamming with Joe Lally, MacKaye's old Fugazi bandmate. That trio became Coriky.

years.cap: The Evens at the Fort Reno 50th birthday show, Washington, July 2018
years.h: Joe Lally sits in, and the Evens become Coriky
years.p: Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina began playing with former Fugazi bassist [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] in 2015. The trio's debut, delayed from March by COVID-19, came out on Dischord in June 2020.
years.xp: The Odds (2012) is still the most recent Evens record.

sources.title: NPR: The Evens, The Power Of Turning Down The Volume (2012)
